skill.name: youtube-channel-api-skill
skill.description: Extract structured YouTube channel search results through the BrowserAct API using keywords and upload date filters.
skill.summary: Find YouTube channels by keyword and return structured creator data through BrowserAct.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill is a straightforward BrowserAct API client for YouTube channel search, with no evidence of prompt injection or malicious intent. The main risks are intentional third-party network access, handling a BrowserAct API key, and guidance that may encourage users to share a secret directly with the agent.

remediation.issue: API key handling guidance may encourage direct secret sharing.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in their local environment or secret manager instead of pasting the key into chat.

remediation.issue: The skill sends user search terms and filters to BrowserAct.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that keywords, upload date filters, and task metadata are processed by BrowserAct before users run the skill.

remediation.issue: The skill executes a local Python script and depends on the requests package.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact command, dependencies, and expected network destination so users can review them before execution.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant YouTube channels manually is slow and inconsistent. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow that returns structured channel details from keyword searches.
actual_capabilities: Runs a Python script that starts a BrowserAct YouTube channel workflow.
Accepts search keywords and an optional upload date filter.
Polls BrowserAct until the workflow finishes or times out.
Returns channel titles, links, handles, subscriber counts, verification status, descriptions, and thumbnails when provided.
Detects missing or invalid BrowserAct API key conditions and reports clear setup guidance.
limitations: Requires a valid BROWSERACT_API_KEY before use.
Sends search inputs and task metadata to the BrowserAct API.
Depends on BrowserAct workflow availability and YouTube result quality.
Long-running tasks can take several minutes and may time out after polling.

Fields suitable for review in a spreadsheet or CRM.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY as an environment variable before running the script.
Use specific keywords to reduce broad or noisy channel results.
Review returned channels manually before outreach or business decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into shared chats or documents.
Do not assume YouTube subscriber data is complete or current without verification.
Do not run repeated broad searches without considering BrowserAct usage limits and privacy needs.

faq.question: What API key does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs BROWSERACT_API_KEY for the BrowserAct workflow API.

faq.question: Does this skill scrape YouTube directly?
faq.answer: No. It calls a BrowserAct workflow that performs the channel search and returns structured results.

faq.question: What inputs can I provide?
faq.answer: Provide search keywords and optionally an upload date filter such as This week or Any time.

faq.question: What data can the output include?
faq.answer: It can include channel title, link, verification status, handle, subscribers, description, and thumbnail URL.

faq.question: Can it run without network access?
faq.answer: No. It requires network access to the BrowserAct API.

faq.question: How should I handle the API key safely?
faq.answer: Store it in the local environment as BROWSERACT_API_KEY and avoid pasting it into chat.
